segments.text: Your agents found the answer. This is the part where you get to see the explanation.

Working across several agents means repeatedly catching up on what each one found. The work is already done. You are the part that is slow, because the finding arrives as a wall of text, a long diff, and a thread you have to rebuild the problem from.
So let it show you instead. The agent turns what it found into a short narrated video, and you follow the problem without reconstructing it in your head first.
It is a plugin. Your agent gets five tools: it creates the video, writes the scenes as real code, narrates them, checks a frame, and renders.
The speech is generated first, with a timestamp on every single word, so every scene length is measured instead of guessed, and the captions are already in sync before one frame has been drawn.

It earns its keep exactly where text is worst. A race condition across three services. Last night's outage. An architecture only two people hold. A handoff from the agent that did the work to the one picking it up.
Setting it up is three commands. Install it, let it fetch a browser and a voice, then connect your agent. Claude Code and Codex both work.
Nothing is uploaded, nothing renders anywhere but your own machine, and all of it is open source.
